name: Author Signals
description: Looks for author attribution (JSON-LD Person/Article.author, microdata, meta tags, byline text) plus E-E-A-T signals: expertise credentials, an author bio or author/about link, and site trust pages (about, contact, privacy, terms, address). AI answer engines weigh who wrote content and whether the site looks accountable when choosing sources to cite.
inputs: document.body.innerText (visible text; first 5000 chars used for credential scan)
element textContent of h2, h3, h4, h5, p, div, section, aside
anchor hrefs (trust and author links, social profile links)

scoring.summary: Page scope. Four additive components capped at 5. Author attribution: +2 if an author name is resolved by any detector (priority JSON-LD, microdata, meta, text pattern), else +1 if an author marker exists without a usable name (meta[name=author] present but empty, microdata author/Person without name, or a JSON-LD Person / article author without a name), else 0. Expertise: +1 if any of 41 expertise regexes matches the combined text (author bio text + schema author jobTitle/description/hasCredential/alumniOf/knowsAbout + first 5000 chars of the body's visible text). Authoritativeness: +1 if an author bio or author link is detected. Trustworthiness: +1 if at least 3 of 5 trust signals are present. Links are matched on the raw href and on the path it resolves to from the page. Score is an integer 0-5.

rules.condition: no authorName but hasAuthorMeta (meta[name="author"] element exists, even with empty content) OR hasMicrodataAuthor (any [itemprop="author"] or [itemtype*="schema.org/Person"] element exists) OR hasSchemaAuthor (a JSON-LD Person, or an Article-like node with an author property, even without a usable name)
rules.note: Plugin sets hasSchemaAuthor for nameless schema authors, so e.g. Article.author {"@id": "https://other/#p"} earns +1.

rules.combined_text: join(" ") of: authorBioText (if any); schemaAuthor.jobTitle; schemaAuthor.description; each hasCredential string or .name; each alumniOf string or .name; each knowsAbout as String(); then document.body.innerText.substring(0, 5000)

rules.hasAuthorBio: true if any of: document has [itemprop="author"]; document has [itemtype*="Person"]; any element matches .author-bio, .about-author, [class*="author-bio"] (selector strings containing author-bio, about-author, itemprop or itemtype); OR authorBioText was captured by author detection (see author_bio_text)
rules.hasAuthorLink: true if any a[href] contains "/author/", "/about", "/contributor/" or "/writer/" in its raw href or in the path it resolves to against the page URL (so href="about.html" counts)
rules.not_counted: Selectors .author-box, [class*="author-box"], .byline, .post-author, .article-author, .contributor, .writer-bio, [rel="author"] set neither flag in detectAuthoritySignals; they only matter through the CSS fallback that can populate authorBioText.

rules.condition: trustScore >= 3, where trustScore counts true values among: link to "/about", "/contact", "/privacy", "/terms" (raw href or resolved path contains it), (address element OR [itemtype*="PostalAddress"])

value: P1 JSON-LD: for each script[type="application/ld+json"], JSON.parse(textContent) (invalid JSON skipped). parseSchemaForAuthor recursively (depth > 5 stops): arrays -> first item with a name wins; node whose @type includes "Person" -> name = extractPersonName (name string trimmed, else givenName + " " + familyName); node whose @type is one of Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle, WebPage, Review, HowTo, Recipe with an author property -> articleHasAuthor = true and name from author (string trimmed, first array element, or Person object name); then @graph items; then, if still no name, any nested object property (excluding @type, @context, @graph) is searched for a Person. So a Person nested anywhere (founder, employee, creator, publisher...) counts as the author. Later script blocks with a name overwrite earlier ones. A non-string name property yields null. Plugin: @type full schema.org IRIs are accepted; pure {"@id"} author references are resolved against nodes on the page; template tags are substituted before parsing (predicted).

P2 microdata (only if no name yet): each [itemprop="author"]: name = textContent of descendant [itemprop="name"], else element textContent trimmed if 2-99 chars; bio text = textContent substring 0-2000 if length > 20. Then, if still no name, [itemtype*="schema.org/Person"] elements with a descendant [itemprop="name"].

P3 meta (always evaluated for hasAuthorMeta): meta[name="author"] content trimmed; else meta[property="article:author"] content; else meta[name="twitter:creator"] content with leading @ stripped. Used only if no name yet.

P4 text patterns (if no name or no bio text): for each authorSectionPatterns regex that matches body visible text (html.mjs innerText approximation), find the FIRST element in document order among h2, h3, h4, h5, p, div, section, aside whose textContent matches; container = el.closest("section, article, aside, div") (can be el itself) or parentElement; if container textContent length is 21-2999 chars it becomes authorBioText; name = capture group of nameFromContainer regex on container text (plugin adds a leading word boundary). Stops at the first pattern that yields bio text.

P5 CSS fallback (only if no bio text): first element (in authoritySelectors order) whose trimmed textContent is 21-2999 chars becomes authorBioText. Link selectors use the same resolved-path matching as trust links.

rules.value: hasSocialProfiles is computed (any a[href] whose resolved href contains one of these) but does NOT affect the score.
experiencePatterns (first-person "in my experience", "I've found", "our team", "hands-on", ...) are matched and reported but do NOT affect the score.

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the integer score: >= 80% (4-5) pass, >= 50% (3) warning, else fail. The extension called 2 a warning; the plugin calls it fail.

detect.source_procedure: Script checks/content/author.mjs runs on every HTML page the site model loads (built output or static HTML) and applies the extension's detectors in order: JSON-LD (lib/jsonld.mjs, template tags substituted), microdata, meta tags, text patterns on the body's visible text (html.mjs innerText approximation), CSS selector fallback; then expertise regexes, authority (bio/author link) and trust (about/contact/privacy/terms links, address). For unbuilt framework sources, build first. Visible text is approximated from static HTML, so client-rendered bylines are not seen.
detect.llm_criteria: Only the text-pattern name extraction (P4) and the expertise scan depend on rendered visible text. The model should: (a) decide whether visible body copy on a content page contains a byline or author section matching the authorSectionPatterns, and extract "By First Last" style names as the regex would (capitalized 2-4 word sequence after By / Written by / Author:, note the regex has no word boundary so "Nearby Coffee Shop" yields "Coffee Shop"); (b) decide whether the first ~5000 visible characters contain any expertise pattern term (degrees, titles like Founder/Director/Editor/Author/Writer, certifications, Certified/Licensed/Registered, Expert/Specialist/Consultant/Professional, "N years of experience", "Member of", "Featured in", etc.). Mirror the regexes, do not apply a stricter human judgement of genuine expertise.

parity.note: Meta tags, JSON-LD, microdata and trust links in templates are reliably detectable from source. Divergence comes from: JSON-LD or meta injected client side (SPA, tag managers, Yoast-like plugins at runtime); template variables whose values live in CMS/frontmatter; the expertise scan and text-pattern detection run on rendered innerText (first 5000 chars, which includes nav/header text) that source can only approximate; href substring matching runs on raw attribute values after framework rendering (e.g. Next.js <Link href="/about">, Hugo relURL output); navigation built from data files or fetched menus. The extension evaluates a single page; source audits must choose which templates represent it.

fix_summary: Add meta name="author" and a JSON-LD Person (name, jobTitle, sameAs, worksFor) as author of an Article/BlogPosting in the head/layout (Astro layout, Hugo head partial, Next.js metadata.authors plus a JSON-LD script, Eleventy base layout, static index.html), add a visible byline/author bio block (class author-bio) and ensure header/footer link to /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms. Real author name, credentials and bio text must come from the user.

divergences.extension: hasSchemaAuthor is only set when a schema author name is found, so a JSON-LD author without a name (e.g. Article.author {"@id": ...} only) never earns the +1 marker point.
divergences.plugin: A JSON-LD Person or an Article-like author property without a usable name sets hasSchemaAuthor and earns +1.
divergences.reason: Bug: the marker branch was unreachable through JSON-LD.

divergences.extension: The authorSectionPatterns /\bby\s+[A-Z][a-z]+\s+[A-Z][a-z]+/i and /about\s+[A-Z][a-z]+/i carry the i flag, so "by the way" and "about this" match, despite comments saying they need capitalized names.
divergences.plugin: Only the leading word is case-insensitive ([Bb]y, [Aa]bout); the name part must be capitalized.
divergences.reason: Comment/code mismatch; false positives on ordinary prose.

divergences.extension: The byline name regex has no leading word boundary, so "Nearby Coffee Shop" yields the author name "Coffee Shop".
Trust and author links use a[href*="/about"] etc. on the raw attribute, so relative links like href="about.html" or "contact.html" do not count.
divergences.plugin: The href is also resolved against the page URL and its path is matched.
divergences.reason: Relative links are equally valid; the extension missed them.

divergences.extension: Pure {"@id"} author references are not resolved; @type must match exactly.
divergences.plugin: Author references are resolved against nodes on the page; a leading http(s)://schema.org/ in @type is stripped.
divergences.reason: Same entity, different JSON-LD spelling (Yoast/Rank Math @graph pattern).

divergences.extension: Reads the rendered page, where template tags are filled in.
divergences.plugin: JSON-LD template tags are replaced by a placeholder; a schema author name that comes from a template is marked predicted.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: template values are unknown in the repo.

divergences.extension: Visible text is document.body.innerText of the rendered page.
divergences.plugin: Visible text is html.mjs innerText (static HTML without script/style/hidden elements).
divergences.reason: Source vs live: no browser rendering.

divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule (2 is fail).

divergences.extension: Credential abbreviations (DO, MA, MS, BA, RN, CPA...) match case-insensitively, so everyday words like "do" earn the expertise point on almost any page.
divergences.plugin: Credential abbreviations match case-sensitively; titles and phrases (Professor, years of experience) stay case-insensitive.
divergences.reason: False positives made the expertise point nearly free.
